items.q: How did Roy Lee go from Columbia expulsion to a funded AI company?
items.a: He built **Interview Coder**, a stealth AI tool that passed Amazon's LeetCode-style interview, posted the stunt publicly, got expelled from Columbia, rode a month of doubt at ~**15K views**, then raised a **$5.3M seed** (Abstract + Susa) and pivoted Cluely to ~**$5M ARR** one month post-launch.

items.q: Why was Interview Coder "a product designed to die"?
items.a: A tool to **cheat on technical interviews** expires the moment interviews change — so the stunt forced a **fast pivot** into a broader multimodal desktop AI overlay pitched as **"cheat on everything."**

items.q: What's broken about Big Tech's LeetCode hiring ritual?
items.a: Candidates memorize **300–600 riddles** for **$200K jobs** — a **20-year practice** with **no job relevance**. Lee's line: **"LeetCode just has nothing to do with what you do on the job."** AI already answers every question, so interviews must go **holistic** (skills + culture).

items.q: What is the translucent AI overlay UX Lee is betting on?
items.a: A **screen-aware, audio-aware translucent overlay** — proactive multimodal interaction instead of chat prompts. "Cheat on everything" reframes AI advantage the way **calculators and spellcheck** were once called cheating.

items.q: What is Lee's X virality rule of thumb?
items.a: ~**1,000 tweets in three months**, with a filter: if **half the world wouldn't hate** the post, it probably won't go viral. **"All press is good press"** — hate drives downloads; get crazier online for the funnel.

items.q: How does he separate online reputation from real life?
items.a: **"Online is not real life."** Keep family in an **unconditional box**; treat Twitter as performance noise, not identity.

sections.title: Risk, moats, and the AI window

items.q: What does "snowball risk-taking" look like in practice?
items.a: Stack incremental bets: **private tool → free post → public stunt → confidential docs**. Downside is smaller and upside larger than founders think — and **2 months of AI play** can put a 19-year-old ahead where biology still needs **10–20 years**.

items.q: Where does Lee see Cluely's lasting moat?
items.a: **Self-hosted models** for latency, cache/condense inputs, custom evals, plus a **personalized model data moat** — usage analytics → hyper-specific fine-tunes per user before incumbents copy the overlay UX.
